claim.pdf_says: In the 7.3.15.2 FLAG-14 general format the glyphs printed WITHOUT an underline are 'ALL' (first outer alternative) and 'ON' (first alternative of the trailing brace). Underlined are '>> FLAG-14', the twelve option names (COMPILE-TIME-ARITHMETIC-EXPRESSIONS, EVALUATE, I-O-DECLARATIVE, I-O-STATUS-04, I-O-STATUS-07, NUM-ED-ZERO-FIGCONST, READ-PREVIOUS, REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH, VALUE-EDITING, VALUE-FIG-CON-LENGTH, VALUE-ZERO, WRITE-END-OF-PAGE) and 'OFF'. Verified by 300 dpi crops of the 'ALL' row and the ON/OFF brace: no rule beneath 'ALL', no rule beneath 'ON', a clear rule beneath 'OFF'.
claim.markdown_says: > **Figure notes (FLAG-14 directive general format syntax diagram).** `FLAG-14`, `ALL`, all twelve option names (`COMPILE-TIME-ARITHMETIC-EXPRESSIONS`, `EVALUATE`, `I-O-DECLARATIVE`, `I-O-STATUS-04`, `I-O-STATUS-07`, `NUM-ED-ZERO-FIGCONST`, `READ-PREVIOUS`, `REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH`, `VALUE-EDITING`, `VALUE-FIG-CON-LENGTH`, `VALUE-ZERO`, `WRITE-END-OF-PAGE`), `ON`, and `OFF` are underlined in the printed standard (required words).  [specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 4401]  It further calls the ON/OFF brace "a separate, required one-of-two selection".
claim.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6 an underlined uppercase word is a REQUIRED word and a non-underlined uppercase word is an OPTIONAL word that may be written or omitted at the user's choice. Promoting ALL and ON to required words is a falsely-restrictive transcription: it makes '>> FLAG-14 EVALUATE' (ON implied) and '>> FLAG-14 ON' read as illegal, and it contradicts 7.3.15.4 GR 2 ("If ON is explicitly or implicitly specified for an option"), which only makes sense because ON is omissible. The note also self-contradicts the sibling FLAG-02 note on page 100, which records the identical glyphs correctly ("`ALL` and `ON` are **not** underlined"). A compiler built from this note would reject legal source and would have no implicit-ON path.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED by direct pixel measurement of the 300 dpi render (E:/Temp/specrecon/v102/spec_p102.png, 2550x3300). I inventoried every solid horizontal rule in the diagram region (y=930..2000, x=340..1900, longest-contiguous-run >= 25 px). Exactly FOURTEEN rules exist: y=1495 x=368..524 (under 'FLAG-14'); twelve rules all beginning at x=689 at y=1148, 1220, 1292, 1364, 1436, 1509, 1581, 1653, 1725, 1797, 1870, 1942 (one under each of the twelve option names); and y=1530 x=1734..1801 (under 'OFF'). NOTHING else. Per-row ink profiles confirm the two negatives directly: 'ALL' occupies y=1000..1028 and the band y=1029..1059 across its full x span (638..700) is ZERO ink -- no underline. 'ON' occupies y=1428..1457 and the band y=1458..1486 across x=1725..1805 is ZERO ink -- no underline. By contrast 'OFF' ends at y=1516 and a 2-px rule of 68 px length with contiguity fraction 1.00 sits at y=1530-1531, i.e. 14 px below its baseline -- exactly where an 'ON' underline would have to be, and is not. The visual crops agree: the ON/OFF brace shows a bare 'ON' above an underscored 'OFF'. So the PDF side of the claim is exactly right, word for word, including which twelve names carry rules. The markdown side is quoted accurately: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 4401 does assert that `ALL` ... `ON`, and `OFF` are 'underlined in the printed standard (required words)', and line 4402 does call the trailing brace 'a separate, required one-of-two selection'. This is a factual misstatement about the printed page, not a formatting, reflow, hyphenation or page-furniture artifact, and it is not recoverable from any adjacent line. It is normative because the underline is the meta-language marker itself: line 2628 ('Keywords ... are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required') versus line 2641 and line 5805 ('uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format'). The claimed self-contradiction is also real and verifiable: the sibling FLAG-02 note at line 4315 records the identical glyph pattern correctly -- '`ALL` and `ON` are **not** underlined' -- and four further sibling notes independently record a non-underlined ON in the very same directive idiom (LISTING line 4613, PROPAGATE line 4742, REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH line 4837, TURN line 4912). Line 4401 is the lone outlier against both the printed page and every sibling transcription. The GR 2 argument holds: 7.3.15.4 GR 2 reads 'If ON is explicitly or implicitly specified for an option', and an implicit-ON path can only exist if ON is omissible, which is precisely what the absent underline encodes. I attempted to refute on every available axis -- text present but reflowed, wrong crop coordinates, an underline just outside the sampled window (my first OFF window did clip its rule at y=1530, which I corrected), a brace stroke mistaken for a rule (my first ALL window did catch a brace at x=630, which I excluded) -- and the finding survived all of them.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, and the claim's description is accurate in every particular I could test; only one downstream inference needs tempering. Confirmed: in the 7.3.15.2 FLAG-14 general format the printed page carries exactly fourteen underline rules -- 'FLAG-14', the twelve option names, and 'OFF'. 'ALL' and 'ON' are printed WITHOUT any underline (measured: zero ink in the entire band beneath each, versus a full-width 2-px rule 14 px below the 'OFF' baseline). The figure note at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 4401 therefore misstates the printed page when it lists `ALL` and `ON` among the words 'underlined in the printed standard (required words)'. Fix: restate line 4401 to list only `FLAG-14`, the twelve option names, and `OFF` as underlined, and add the explicit negative '`ALL` and `ON` are **not** underlined', matching the sibling FLAG-02 note at line 4315 verbatim in form. Line 4402's phrase 'a separate, required one-of-two selection' should likewise be corrected: because `ON` is an optional word, the trailing brace is satisfied by writing `OFF`, by writing `ON`, or by writing neither -- omission being equivalent to ON, which is exactly the 'implicitly specified' path 7.3.15.4 GR 2 depends on. One refinement to the claim: its example '>> FLAG-14 ON' (omitting `ALL`) is a weaker inference than the ON case. 7.3.15.4 GR 4 a) assigns `ALL` distinct semantics ('ALL. All of the options apply.'), so a genuinely omissible `ALL` would leave that outer alternative empty; ISO's non-underlining of `ALL` here is more plausibly a typesetting defect than a real optional-word marker. The transcription's duty is nevertheless to record the glyphs AS PRINTED and flag the anomaly rather than silently 'repair' it by adding an underline -- which is precisely the pattern the LISTING note at line 4613 already follows ('the missing underline appears to be a typesetting omission in the standard and is reproduced here as printed'). The implicit-ON consequence, by contrast, is solid and normative: a compiler built from line 4401 as written would reject the legal '>> FLAG-14 EVALUATE' and would have no implicit-ON path at all.
